{"additions":827,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjI2OTQwNTEx","is_bot":false,"login":"Beehtrix","name":""},"baseRefName":"main","body":"Related to #412 and #534. Not marked as fixing them: #557 already fixed the main symptom (compact transcripts reading as empty), and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

This is rebased onto `main` 6c4b11de and merges cleanly with current `main` (fb99b029). That brings in #575's split scan-cache versions, #589's privacy-layer removal and #590's flat fact store. I adjusted the versioning to fit, as described below. If you'd rather not take it, or want it split, say so and I'll adjust or close it.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers: I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## What #557 already does

It reads top-level `content` for compact records in the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers. Two of my new tests (`TestScanConversationCompactTranscript`, `TestHistoryIndexesDefaultCompactExport`) pass on unmodified main.

## What this PR still adds

Three of my new tests still fail on main 6c4b11de (re-run after the rebase): `TestExtractHistoryJSONFragmentsCompactTranscript`, `TestHistoryIndexBuildsRecordsFromCompactTranscript` and `TestHistoryDeltaRescansOverlayFromPreCompactReader`.

- **Tool output in code facts.** Compact transcripts inline tool output as `tool_use.result.output`, with no separate `tool_result` record. `extractContentFragments` now mines it, so compact sessions get code facts. Native transcripts have no `result` key, so nothing changes for them.
- **Rebuild stale history indexes.** The history source manifest stores `extraction_version`, and `historyIndexCurrent` treats an index built with another version as stale. Without it, a plain `refresh` with unchanged transcripts keeps an index built by an older reader. Manifests from older binaries have no field, read as 0 and rebuild once.
- **Scan cache: only the extractor revision moves.** #575 split the scan cache into a wire version (10, which released clients still read) and `extractor_version`. This PR moves only the extractor revision, `historyScanCacheVersion` 11 → 13. `historyScanCacheWireVersion` stays 10.
  - Revision 12 mines compact tool output, because a revision-11 cache holds scans with no code facts.
  - Revision 13 covers the null/empty `message` fallback below. Earlier builds of this branch wrote revision 12 without that fallback, and their caches would otherwise stay current. I confirmed this with a run: a brain built by one of those builds kept 0 exchanges after a refresh at revision 12, and gets 2 at 13 (`TestHistoryRefreshRescansRevision12NullMessageCache`, with a real fixture).
  - `TestHistoryScanCacheWireCompatibilityAndExtractionInvalidation` follows the constant now.
  - `TestHistoryScanCachePreviousExtractorRevisionRescans` checks that a cache from the previous revision is rescanned rather than reused.
  - `docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md` now says revision 13.
- **Short-term overlay: format stays 3 and gains `extractor_version`.** An earlier version of this PR bumped `historyShortTermVersion` 3 → 4 instead. That made every existing v3 overlay load as unsupported on upgrade, so recent sessions held only in the overlay fell back to the long-term index until the next delta. A build without the change also couldn't read a v4 overlay. I confirmed both by running them. Now the overlay keeps format 3 and records the extraction revision. A delta carries an unchanged file's entry forward only when the overlay's `extractor_version` matches the current revision. So an old overlay with an empty entry for a compact transcript is still readable, and that file is re-parsed on the next delta. Removing the reuse check, or not writing the field, each makes `TestHistoryDeltaRescansOverlayFromPreCompactReader` fail. Until that delta runs, the overlay doesn't count as complete coverage. Otherwise `doctor` would say "short-term memory covers the gap" for entries an older extractor built. Instead it reports partial coverage and names `refresh delta`, which `TestShortTermOverlayStatesNeverClaimCoverage` checks.
  - Only earlier builds of this branch ever wrote version 4 (no main commit or release did). Such an overlay has the v3 layout without `extractor_version`, so it's now read as v3 with an unknown extractor: it stays in retrieval, isn't counted as complete, and the next delta rewrites it as v3. Before this, the overlay loaded as unsupported and doctor said to upgrade. `TestHistoryShortTermReadsLegacyV4Overlay` uses a real overlay written by one of those builds. Version 4 is reserved now, so the "unknown newer overlay" health test uses 5.
- **Doctor flags an index from an older extractor.** `history_freshness` used to compare only session fingerprints, so it said "built from the current exported sessions" for an index that `refresh` would rebuild. It now warns and names `refresh` (`TestDoctorHistoryFreshnessFlagsOlderExtractor`). The warning, and the overlay's partial-coverage text, give the revision and say whether it's older or newer than this binary's. Before, data from a newer binary was also called "older". Behaviour is unchanged: any other revision is re-parsed, as with the scan cache.
- **One shared helper.** `transcriptRecordContent` returns a `user`/`assistant` record's content in either shape (nested under `message`, otherwise top-level `content`). It replaces the separate fallbacks #557 added in each reader. Those fallbacks disagreed on an edge case: `"message":{}` or `null`. A null or empty `message` now counts as absent, and `TestTranscriptRecordContentPrecedence` pins the order.

## Commits

1. fix(history): read compact v1 transcripts in history and conversation readers
2. fix: Version persisted history indexes
3. fix(history): invalidate short-term overlays from the pre-compact reader
4. fix(history): treat a null or empty message as absent in transcriptRecordContent
5. fix(history): keep the overlay format at v3 and gate reuse on extractor_version
6. fix(history): don't count an older extractor's overlay as complete coverage
7. fix(history): keep v4 overlays from the pre-release build readable
8. fix(history): move the extraction revision to 13 for the null-message fallback
9. fix(doctor): flag a history index built by an older extractor
10. fix(doctor): name a newer extractor revision as newer, not older

Commit 5 reverses commit 3's version bump while keeping its test, and commits 6–10 follow from review of that. I can squash them if you prefer.

## Tests

The new tests are in `internal/cli/history_compact_transcript_test.go`, with fixtures written by hand from the format spec for claude-code, codex and pi.

Everything below was run at f66dbe8c in a clean `env -i` environment (Linux amd64, go 1.27.3):

- `mise run lint` passes.
- `mise run test:prepush` passes (`go test ./... -count=1`, gofmt, vet).
- `go test -race -count=1` passes on `./internal/cli/`, `./internal/cli/internal/manifest/` and `./internal/cli/patterns/`.

## Upgrade cost: one rescan

Moving the extractor revision to 13 makes every existing brain rescan its transcripts once and rebuild its history index on the next `refresh`. That covers released brains at revision 11 and brains built by earlier builds of this branch at revision 12. It's the same one-time cost as any extractor-revision bump. Overlays from another revision stay readable and are re-parsed by the next `refresh delta`.

## Compatibility notes

- **Released clients.** I built v0.4.0 from its pinned commit. Once a current build writes a brain, its manifest is schema 5 (#590), and v0.4.0's `privacy verify` and `refresh delta` already refuse that brain with `memory_unsupported_version`. So the overlay and scan-cache changes here don't add a new break for released clients.
- **The new `extraction_version` manifest field.** A build from after #590 but before this PR can't rewrite a manifest that has the field, because `LoadForReplace` rejects unknown fields. I confirmed this by running it. Readers ignore the field. Main has added manifest fields the same way without a schema bump, so I left it. #564 adds the same kind of field to the pattern source.

## What was NOT verified

- The unit-test fixtures were written by hand from the spec and the CLI's converter source, not captured from a live `entire` checkpoint.
- Real data, run before the rebase on the earlier head against main f8deab17 and not repeated: real compact checkpoints from entire-brain's own refs (newest 400: 91 Claude Code, 5 Codex, 7 Pi sessions). History records went from 101,957 to 142,657. Only code-fact records changed: Claude Code 20,770 → 59,164, Pi 369 → 2,675. Codex and all other record kinds were unchanged.
- Upgrading a real v0.4.0-built brain was also run before the rebase only.
- `-race` covered only the three packages above. Not run on macOS or Windows.
- Watch alone doesn't rebuild an index from an older extractor when sessions are unchanged. Memory reconciliation goes by session input digests (0 jobs created in a run on the revision-12 fixture), so only `refresh` rebuilds the index. The same is true on main for its 10 → 11 bump. Not changed here; doctor now says to run `refresh`.
- After upgrading, `refresh delta` can treat every transcript as short-term material and fill the capped overlay until a full `refresh` consolidates. This happens on every extractor-revision bump. Not changed here.

## Relation to #564

#564 fixes the other readers (`episode_tools.go`, `recall_evidence_source.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`). It's based on `main` and doesn't depend on this PR. Both are rebased onto 6c4b11de, `git merge-tree` of the two is clean, and on the merged tree `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` passed at b7b4fb55 (not re-run since). On fb99b029 merged with this branch, `go test ./internal/cli/...` passes at f66dbe8c, and `scripts/test-memory-storage-compat.sh` (v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0) passed at 84e9f6df (the later commits change only doctor and its messages).

**TLDR: PR #560 is still needed, it is not superseded, and it passes its tests against current main. The only merge conflict is one docs file. I recommend you take it after a rebase.**

The link points to Beehtrix's comment on issue #412 (history index stays empty). They opened PR #560 and ask if you want it narrowed or closed.

What I verified:

- **Your #557 (merged Oct 29) fixed the main symptom** — compact `v:1` transcripts reading as 0 records / 0 exchanges. The PR correctly claims only the remainder.
- **Main still lacks the PR's changes.** On current main, `tool_use` blocks ignore the compact dialect's inlined `result.output` (`internal/cli/history.go:2163`), so compact sessions lose tool-output code facts. `historyScanCacheVersion` is still 11, there is no `extraction_version` manifest field, and the `transcriptRecordContent` helper is absent. Their real-data run showed Claude Code code-fact records go from ~20k to ~59k.
- **The conflict is trivial.** GitHub marks the PR CONFLICTING, but a merge with current main conflicts only in `docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md`. All Go files auto-merge.
- **Tests pass on the merged tree.** I built the merge of current main (15bc2373) and the PR, and ran the 8 new tests (compact fragment extraction, extractor-revision rescan, overlay v4 compat, doctor freshness). All pass in 1.4s.
- **Related items:** companion PR #564 (other readers) is still open and independent. Issues #412, #534, and #411 are all still open. CI gates on the PR are neutral; only Copilot has commented.

One caveat: the PR bumps the extractor revision to 13, so every existing brain rescans and rebuilds its history index on the next `refresh`. That is the normal one-time cost of a revision bump.

Notes on my checks: Brain preflight passed (dev build, keyword retrieval only). A `recall` for prior decisions on this topic returned no facts, so I verified everything against source and tests directly. The recall also warned the local manifest is behind the store and suggests `entire brain refresh`.

Suggested reply to Beehtrix: keep the PR as-is (no narrowing), ask for a rebase to resolve the docs conflict, then review. I can post that reply, or do a full code review of the PR first — tell me which.

# Review PR

Review a pull request with structured, actionable feedback.

## Arguments

- `` — PR number, URL, or branch name. If empty, review the current branch's open PR.

## Process

### 1. Fetch PR context

```
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,commits,author
gh pr diff <pr>
```

Read the PR description carefully — it defines scope and intent. Everything you review should be evaluated against what the PR is trying to accomplish.

### 2. Understand the change

Before reviewing line-by-line:
- What is this PR doing and why?
- What files are touched and what's the blast radius?
- Are there any architectural implications?

### 3. Review with this checklist

**Correctness**
- Does the code do what the PR description says?
- Are there logic errors, off-by-one bugs, or unhandled edge cases?
- Are error paths handled correctly?

**Security**
- Any injection risks (SQL, XSS, command injection)?
- Are secrets, tokens, or credentials handled safely?
- Are inputs validated at system boundaries?

**Testing**
- Are there tests for the new/changed behavior?
- Do tests cover edge cases, not just the happy path?
- Are test assertions meaningful (not just "doesn't throw")?

**Design**
- Does the change follow existing codebase patterns and conventions?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over/under-engineered)?
- Are there unnecessary changes outside the stated scope?

**Performance**
- Any N+1 queries, unbounded loops, or missing pagination?
- Are there opportunities for batching or caching that were missed?
- Will this scale with the data sizes it will encounter?

**Readability**
- Are names clear and consistent with the codebase?
- Is complex logic adequately explained?
- Would a future reader understand the "why" behind non-obvious decisions?

### 4. Adversarial review

Take a second, adversarial pass over the diff. Actively try to break the change — assume it has flaws and hunt for them across:

- **Performance** — worst-case inputs, hot paths, allocations, contention.
- **Stability** — race conditions, partial failures, retries, resource leaks, crash recovery.
- **Correctness** — inputs and states that violate the author's assumptions.
- **Simplicity** — code that could be deleted or replaced with something simpler/stdlib.
- **Platform design standards** — deviations from the platform's established design patterns and conventions.

Add any findings to the output using the same severity format.

### 5. Run /simplify

Run the `/simplify` skill (via the Skill tool) against the changed code and fold its findings into the review output.

### 6. Structure your output

For each finding, use this format:

**[severity] file:line — short title**
Description of the issue and why it matters. Include a suggested fix when possible.

Severity levels:
- **[blocking]** — Must fix before merge. Correctness bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
- **[important]** — Should fix. Design problems, missing tests for critical paths, performance issues.
- **[nit]** — Nice to fix. Style, naming, minor improvements. Don't block merge on these.
- **[question]** — Not necessarily wrong, but needs clarification or discussion.

### 7. Summary

End with a brief summary:
- Overall assessment (approve / request changes / needs discussion)
- What the PR does well
- Top 1-3 items that need attention
- Any scope concerns (changes that seem unrelated to the stated goal)

## Guidelines

- Review what's in the diff, not what you wish was there. Don't request unrelated refactoring.
- If the PR is large, focus on the most impactful files first.
- Be specific — "this could be better" is not useful. Show what "better" looks like.
- Distinguish between "this is wrong" and "I would do this differently." Only the former is blocking.
- If you're unsure about something, use [question] severity instead of asserting it's wrong.
- Read relevant source files (not just the diff) when you need context about how changed code integrates with the rest of the system.

# Review: PR #560 — fix(history): mine compact tool output, rebuild stale history indexes, share one transcript-content helper

Reviewed against current `main` (15bc2373). Author: Beehtrix (external contributor). 827 additions / 46 deletions, 24 files, all in `internal/cli` plus one docs page.

## What I verified (not just read)

- **The PR is still necessary.** Main's `tool_use` case ignores the compact dialect's inlined `result.output`, main is still at scan-cache revision 11, and the manifest has no `extraction_version` field. #557 fixed only the empty-content symptom.
- **The mining reads the correct field.** The ETF spec (`entireio/cli` `transcript/README.md`) defines `result` as `{"output": string, "status": ...}` — `output` is always a string, which is exactly what `jsonString(jsonMap(block["result"])["output"])` reads. A missing `result` degrades to a no-op for native transcripts.
- **It merges and passes on today's main.** I built the merge locally: the only conflict is `docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md`. On the merged tree, all 8 new tests pass, the full `go test ./internal/cli/...` suite exits 0, and `gofmt -s` and `go vet` are clean.
- **No hidden writers or readers were missed.** Graph confirms `saveHistoryShortTerm` has one caller, the overlay readers all go through the two loaders (both normalize legacy v4), and `historySourceManifest` has one production constructor, which sets `ExtractionVersion`.

## Findings

**[important] rebase required — docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md**
GitHub marks the PR CONFLICTING. The Go files auto-merge; only this docs file conflicts. Ask for a rebase before merge.

**[important] internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:2097 — the PR leaves one diverging copy of the dialect rule it centralizes**
`distillConversationText` keeps `if message, ok := obj["message"]; ok { ... }` — key presence, not emptiness. A record with `"message": null` (the exact shape the revision-13 bump and the `history_brain_rev12_null_message` fixture exist for) now indexes correctly but still distills to `""`. The shared helper is one file away: `distillTextBlocks(transcriptRecordContent(obj))`. Either fold it into this PR or make sure #564 covers it; today neither does.

**[question] internal/cli/history_delta.go:245-263 — is the legacy-v4 overlay shim worth keeping forever?**
The v4 stamp was written only by pre-release builds of this branch; no main commit or release shipped it. The overlay is documented as disposable, and the existing `unsupported` path already rebuilds it on the next delta at the cost of minutes of short-term coverage. The shim instead adds `normalizeLegacyShortTerm`, `readableShortTermVersion`, a permanently reserved version number, a test file, and a fixture. Dropping it would delete roughly 80 lines and one implicit coupling (`memory_admin.go:680` is correct only because `loadHistoryShortTermRaw` normalized upstream). Your call — the code as written is correct and tested — but deletion looks like the better trade.

**[nit] internal/cli/history_delta.go:182-243 — loader prologue duplicated**
`loadHistoryShortTermState` and `loadHistoryShortTermRaw` share a verbatim read/unmarshal/normalize prologue; this PR had to apply the same two edits to each. One shared parse helper would prevent drift.

**[nit] internal/cli/history_delta.go:265 — the revision is stamped twice**
`saveHistoryShortTerm` force-stamps `Version` and `ExtractorVersion`, but its only caller already sets both at construction, and `complete()` depends on the construction-time value. Pick one stamping point. Related: `readableShortTermVersion`'s comment says it serves "the loaders", but only `memoryOverlayHealth` calls it.

**[nit] internal/cli/history_cache_compat_test.go:227 and history_compact_transcript_test.go:520 — tests re-implement existing helpers**
The new scan-cache test hand-rolls gzip+write that `saveHistoryScanCache` already does (and the PR's own overlay test uses it); the export test duplicates ~40 lines of `filelessCheckpointFixtureWithTranscript`. Both would shrink by reusing the helpers.

**[nit] internal/cli/history.go:135 — `historyScanCacheVersion` is now a misnomer**
The constant also stamps the manifest and the overlay. Renaming it (e.g. `historyExtractionRevision`) and keeping the full rule's prose in one place (the const block currently shares it with the manifest field and the helper comment) would stop three copies from drifting. The `transcriptRecordContent` comment also carries git-history prose that can go.

**[nit] internal/cli/history.go:2209 — unbounded `strings.Split` on mined tool output**
`extractToolResultFacts` allocates a slice of every line of a possibly huge `result.output` even though it stops at 8 fragments. Same shape as the pre-existing `function_call_output` path, so consistent — just newly exercised on bigger inputs.

## Summary

**Assessment: approve after a rebase; the nits are optional.** No blocking or correctness issues. The core design is at the right depth: one shared helper for the dialect rule, and extractor-revision gating that fixes the general class of "parser changes are invisible to content-based caches" rather than patching revision 12. Test quality is high — real upgrade fixtures, leak assertions, per-agent coverage, and honest "not verified" notes in the PR body.

One cost to accept knowingly: revision 13 forces every existing brain to rescan transcripts on its next `refresh` — the normal one-time cost of an extractor bump.
